content: Staphylococcus haemolyticus is a bacterial species classified under the genus Staphylococcus. It is a Gram-positive coccus, coagulase-negative, and catalase-positive organism. This bacterium is commonly found as a commensal microorganism on the skin of humans and animals. However, it is an infrequent cause of soft-tissue infections, typically occurring in immunocompromised individuals. Staphylococcus haemolyticus exhibits resistance to multiple antimicrobial agents, including vancomycin in some cases. This vancomycin resistance is particularly concerning as it has the potential to be transferred to other, more pathogenic staphylococcal species. Treatment Guidelines: Antimicrobial Regimens for Coagulase-Negative Staphylococcus (CoNS), including Staphylococcus epidermidis: 1. Methicillin-Sensitive Staphylococcus epidermidis (MSSE): Preferred Regimens: 1. Oxacillin 1–2 g IV every 4 hours. 2. Nafcillin 1–2 g IV every 4 hours. 3. Cephalothin. Alternative Regimen: Rifampin 600 mg/day orally once daily, combined with Sulfamethoxazole and Trimethoprim (or Fluoroquinolones), and Daptomycin 600 mg orally or IV every 12 hours. Note: Approximately 75% of Staphylococcus epidermidis isolates are methicillin-resistant. 2. Methicillin-Resistant Staphylococcus epidermidis (MRSE): Preferred Regimen: Vancomycin 1 g IV every 12 hours, with or without Rifampin 600 mg/day orally once daily. Note: For deep-seated infections, consider adding Gentamicin, with or without Rifampin 600 mg/day orally once daily, to the treatment regimen. 3. Prosthetic Device Infections: Preferred Regimen: Oxacillin 1–2 g IV every 4 hours (or Vancomycin 1 g IV every 12 hours), combined with Rifampin 600 mg/day orally once daily and Gentamicin 3 mg/kg/day IV or IM every 8–24 hours. Note: The duration of therapy depends on the site and severity of the infection.
